title: CONTINUOUS TERRAIN: RAMP AND LOW GRIP
subtitle: Inspect the slope, contact, traction estimate, and honest failure modes.
briefing: The authored surface is continuous; its height, contact, and material are owned by SIM.
ROBOT sees motion, IMU, wheel feedback, and LiDAR residuals, not friction or terrain truth.
A failed climb is a valid result when the measured traction budget cannot make it safe.

prediction.question: What should a robust robot do when measured slip reduces its grip estimate?

choices.label: Reduce speed and preserve a safe stopping margin
choices.explanation: The grip governor uses measured residuals and keeps the safety footprint unchanged.

choices.label: Read SIM material friction directly
choices.explanation: Terrain and material truth never cross into ROBOT.

choices.label: Increase command until the wheels dig through
choices.explanation: More demand cannot make an unsafe contact envelope safe.

running_prompt: Use Engineering view to inspect contact/slip evidence and the ROBOT grip belief; K remains a SIM-only review layer.

lessons: Continuous terrain is part of the plant, not a render-time height offset.
Slip and normal load drive presentation effects, while ROBOT receives only its measured interfaces.
Safety is evaluated before smoothness or completion time.
